lines: Every ride you finish now earns XP, worked out by the backend.
Hold your power within ten percent of the target, in a race or a class, and those seconds count. The share goes with the ride.
Back comes the XP, line by line: a hundred for finishing, twenty for each rider you beat, seventy-five for the podium, and your time on target.
Second of ten against bots, eighty-four percent on target: four hundred and two. When streaks arrive, a four-day streak makes it four forty-two.
A solo race or a class has no place to win. A ride that doesn't finish earns nothing. And sending a ride twice never pays twice.
What the tests prove: every line of the rule, through the API and in the calculator, and the share sent from the ride.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
